description:
The maintainer committed four ENDF/B-VIII.0 thermal tapes on 2026-08-14 (commit ffef0fb76f): tsl-CinSiC, tsl-crystalline-graphite, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P, tsl-reactor-graphite-30P. tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) was NOT among them.

CONSEQUENCE. Carbon in 3C-SiC now has a usable coherent-elastic channel from its tape (2.94078 b at 0.0253 eV, see op-t33q). Silicon in 3C-SiC does not: regenerating tsl-SiinSiC from its embedded deck gives elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367 = 0.06367 b against a free-gas Si-28 value of 1.9914 b, i.e. -96.8%. A TRISO SiC layer wired today would be correct on its carbon half and 3% of the truth on its silicon half.

NEEDED. tsl-SiinSiC.endf from the same ENDF/B-VIII.0 thermal_scatt source (https://www.nndc.bnl.gov/endf-b8.0/download.html), dropped into reference-data/endf/ with its row filled in the README provenance table (a placeholder row is already there). Maintainer said on 2026-08-17 they would upload it.

Note this environment cannot fetch it: GH issue #21 records that the egress policy denies www-nds.iaea.org (403), which is why these tapes are committed rather than downloaded.

Blocks a physically correct TRISO SiC layer alongside op-t33q.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
SUPPLIED 2026-08-17. The maintainer pushed tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43, ZA=143, AWR=27.844, 7,243,180 B) plus the evaluator's tsl-SiinSiC.readme in commit cdbea87c9e. Both were landed under crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/decks/ -- inside the `include` allowlist, so unlike the old tests/resources/ location they would have shipped -- and were relocated to reference-data/endf/ in 605d7a7383. Provenance rows filled in.

Measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:
  Si in SiC: elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.06615 = 3.00693  (free-gas Si-28 1.9914 -> +51.0%)
against the deck-regenerated 0.00000 + 0.06367 = 0.06367 (-96.8%). The elastic channel is present and the bound law is now above the free-gas value, as a bound crystalline scatterer should be.

FINDING, and it is the one that matters for whoever wires the SiC layer: MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry BYTE-IDENTICAL MF=7/MT=2 sections -- 1044 records each, differing only in the header line's ZA/AWR (verified by extracting MT=2 from both tapes and diffing columns 1-66; 1043 of 1044 lines match exactly). Not a parser bug and not an evaluator error: coherent elastic scattering is a property of the 3C-SiC lattice as a whole, not of one sublattice, so one structure factor is delivered in both materials.

Consequence: a transport code that builds a SiC region from both S(alpha,beta) materials and sums their elastic channels DOUBLE-COUNTS the Bragg scattering. MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once -- assigned to one sublattice or split -- not carried by both nuclides. Written up in reference-data/endf/README.md.

Closing: the tape is here. The double-counting question belongs to op-t33q / op-6tz.35 where the layer actually gets wired.

title: reference-data: tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) still missing -- silicon half of the TRISO SiC layer has no elastic channel

description:
Branch `claude/outram-park-backend-51qhi6` (last commit 003e402a53, 2026-06-27) is the ONLY branch in the repo carrying content that never reached `develop`. Its other two commits (the TAMPINES near-saturation x~0 HEM choked-flow fix, 06e33fb0db / 4f57b80332) ARE already on develop by a different route — verified by grepping develop for `saturation_line_sonic_mass_flux`, `quality_bubble_point_subcooled` and `diagnose_bubble_point_artifact`, all present. So only the README section is unmerged.

The stranded content is a 57-line '## Note on AI-assisted development cost vs. value' section for the root README: a price table, a ~\$600 conservative upper bound, a \$2,400-\$12,000 human-equivalent comparison (3-10 specialist engineer-days at \$120-250/hr), and an augmentation-not-replacement caveat.

It is stale in two ways:
1. The model names and prices are Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.8 era.
2. More importantly, the \$600 figure was an ESTIMATE made because 'token usage was not metered precisely here'. That is no longer true: `crates/kovan-metrics` now writes per-commit `API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit` trailers and `kovan tokens query --from DDMMYY --to DDMMYY` sums the real measured usage from the git record. Publishing the old guess alongside a working measurement pipeline would be an overclaim in the wrong direction.

Maintainer decision needed, three options:
- (a) Drop it. Let the branch die; the kovan-metrics trailers plus the historian reports are the honest accounting.
- (b) Port it with real numbers - re-derive the cost from `kovan tokens query` over the actual window, keep the human-comparison and the augmentation caveat prose, refresh the model table.
- (c) Port verbatim as a dated historical note, clearly marked as a June-2026 estimate superseded by measured data.

Recommendation: (b) or (c). The augmentation-not-replacement caveat and the 'no verification oracle = not safe' point are genuinely good writing and are worth keeping regardless; it is only the dollar figure that is unsupported now.

Also recorded from the same branch audit (no action filed, maintainer call): five branches are fully merged into develop with zero unique content and could be deleted - `claude/boon-lay-branch-m8wmns`, `claude/kovan-feature-5b9xu8`, `claude/outram-blender-mggk7u`, `claude/outram-foam-8ookor`, `claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9`, `claude/outram-park-backend-31s8p8`. `claude/pflortran-merge-develop-8k3wji` is 13 commits ahead but every one is a merge-from-develop and its diff against develop is EMPTY, so it too carries no work. `claude/digital-twin-engine-vfseuf` was 1 ahead (coolprop (rho,h) backward-solve seeding) and has since been merged into develop as d46e7434e5.
title: README AI cost-vs-value note is stranded on claude/outram-park-backend-51qhi6 and is stale

description: From DWSIM Expander.vb -- DWSIM's turbine/expander model, basis for tampines::components::Turbine (op-dt3.4). Isentropic (PS-flash) ideal outlet state, adiabatic-efficiency-corrected real outlet, iterative Schultz polytropic-efficiency correction factor (ASME PTC-10-style, mutual dependence between polytropic/adiabatic efficiency resolved by fixed-point iteration). description:
The workspace CLAUDE.md's own 'Workflow rules' section already names this gap: the harness's built-in rust-analyzer LSP tool is READ-ONLY (goToDefinition/findReferences/hover/documentSymbol/workspaceSymbol/call hierarchy) and explicitly does NOT expose rename/code-action/applyEdit -- an agent using only that tool has no way to drive an actual refactor, and CLAUDE.md currently tells an agent to reach for 'kopitiam rename'/'kopitiam code-actions' to fill it (with the caveat that kopitiam rename is itself broken upstream right now -- kopitiam#30, 'Client does not support rename capability').

kopitiam-semantic's RustAnalyzerSession (already a kovan-cli dependency as of op-l3uz's def/sig/refs work) already has the session-level methods needed: rename(file, line, character, new_name) -> Vec<FileEdit>, code_actions(file, line, character) -> Vec<CodeAction>, apply_code_action(action) -> Vec<FileEdit>. kopitiam's own apps/cli/src/rename.rs and code_actions.rs are the reference CLI wiring (diff-preview by default, --apply to write, per this workspace's own kopitiam-rename-preference note in CLAUDE.md).

PROPOSED SHAPE (not yet built):
- kovan-cli rename <symbol> --file <file> --new-name <name> [--apply] -- name-based like def/sig/refs (resolve via document_symbols, same as op-l3uz), diff preview unless --apply.
- kovan-cli code-actions <file> <line> <character> [--apply <index>] -- list available code actions at a position, apply one by index with --apply.
- WATCH: kopitiam's own rename is currently broken upstream (kopitiam#30 -- rust-analyzer rejects the rename request with LSP error -32803, 'Client does not support rename capability', because kopitiam-semantic's initialize handshake doesn't declare the textDocument.rename client capability). Since kovan-cli would depend on the SAME kopitiam-semantic crate and its LspClient, this exact bug is very likely inherited unchanged -- verify against a live session BEFORE claiming this feature works, don't assume it's fine just because it's a different CLI wrapping the same library. If it reproduces here, this bead is blocked on that upstream fix landing (kopitiam#30), not implementable as a workaround from this workspace (kopitiam is consume-binaries/libraries-only, never patched here).
- Depends on the keep-warm daemon design (sibling bead) being at least considered together, since rename/code-actions are exactly the kind of interactive, multi-step workflow (list actions, then apply one) where a cold rust-analyzer restart per step would be worst.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: VERIFIED 2026-08-22 (before this bead's speculative caveat was written, corrected here): tested kopitiam_semantic::RustAnalyzerSession::rename directly (a throwaway example, computed-only -- rename() never writes to disk per its own doc comment, confirmed via git status showing zero changes) against this workspace's rust-analyzer. It WORKS -- 2 file edits computed successfully, no LSP -32803 capability error. kopitiam#30's 'Client does not support rename capability' bug is therefore specific to the kopitiam CLI BINARY's own session/capability setup (apps/cli's layer), NOT to kopitiam-semantic::RustAnalyzerSession itself, which kovan-cli would call directly. Correction to this bead's original description: do NOT assume kovan-cli rename is blocked on kopitiam#30 -- it is not, verified. The 'WATCH' paragraph in this bead's original description is superseded by this note.

title: kovan-cli: rename + code-actions commands (rust-analyzer-backed) -- fills the gap the harness's read-only LSP tool leaves
